mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary policy that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5% and rises by more than 0.25 percentage points in a single month, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and FEDFUNDS rise > 0.25pp in 1 month
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC exceeds 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and an increase in consumer credit (RSAFS) indicates a weakening housing market and rising consumer debt, which together signal reduced consumer spending power and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST declines and RSAFS increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising labor force participation rate (PAYEMS growth > 0.5% monthly) signals strong labor market conditions that boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past quarter indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO increases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% year-over-year and housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1900 thousand units, it signals inflationary pressures and a cooling housing market, which together cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a decline in the money supply (RSAFS) indicates a tightening monetary policy that reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and RSAFS falls, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In a high industrial production growth regime (INDPRO > 110.0), a decline in manufacturing output (INDPRO) signals a potential supply shock that disrupts corporate production and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 110.0 and INDPRO declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
